name: Scale and Observability
summary: What happens when the system grows — and how to see what is actually going on.
prerequisites: Requires architecture — there is nothing to scale before the system has a shape.
syllabus: Scaling databases: indexes, replicas, sharding and the CAP theorem
NoSQL databases: document, key-value, column, graph and time series
Mitigation strategies: throttling, backpressure, circuit breaker
topics: Vertical and horizontal scaling: the limit of each
The CAP theorem and eventual consistency
NoSQL by family: document, key-value, wide column, graph and time series
MongoDB, DynamoDB, Cassandra, Neo4j and InfluxDB
Migrations and schema changes without stopping the system
Instrumenting the application: metrics, logs and traces
Retries with exponential backoff and jitter
